issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: An overheating warning, coolant that keeps disappearing with no puddle, milky or brown oil, or an engine that overheats after shutdown and will not restart.
issues.why: Both V6 engines use a water pump mounted inside the engine behind the timing chain. When its seal fails, coolant can leak into the oil, where it can quickly ruin the engine bearings. Owners report failures from about 50,000 miles on.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often. If it drops for no visible reason or the oil looks milky, stop driving and get a pressure test. Early repair can prevent the need for a new engine.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit (PTU) overheats, leaks or fails
issues.sym: A propane-like or burning smell at idle, gear oil leaking onto the exhaust, or a clucking, rattling or grinding noise from the front of the car on AWD models.
issues.why: The PTU is a small gearbox that sends power to the rear wheels. It sits beside the hot exhaust with very little fluid, so the fluid can cook and break down and the bearings and seals wear. Ford released bulletins and a bearing repair kit for this.
issues.next: Have the PTU inspected at the first sign of a smell or leak, and consider changing its fluid periodically. A noisy PTU usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: PTU leaks fluid because its vent hose is missing
issues.sym: Oily residue or drips around the power transfer unit at the front of the transmission on an AWD car.
issues.why: On some 2013-2014 AWD cars built before mid-December 2013, the PTU vent hose was missing or came off, letting fluid escape through the vent.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the vent hose. Installing a new hose and topping up the fluid is a quick fix, and it protects the PTU from running low.

issues.t: Sudden power loss from a failing throttle body
issues.sym: The car suddenly will not accelerate, a wrench or service-engine warning appears, and the engine may run only at low power. Some owners report brief stalls.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body or its sensors can fail, and the engine computer then limits power to protect the engine.
issues.next: Get off the road safely. Have the codes read; replacing the throttle body is a common fix. Ask whether any extended warranty applies.

issues.t: EcoBoost turbo fails with smoke and power loss
issues.sym: A loud whirring or whistling, blue or white smoke from the exhaust, and loss of power or shaking on the highway.
issues.why: Owner reports describe turbochargers failing on the twin-turbo engine, sometimes along with internal engine damage.
issues.next: Stop driving if there is heavy smoke, since a failed turbo can feed oil into the engine. Get a diagnosis before replacing parts; check oil level often.

issues.t: Loud clicking from the timing chain area at startup
issues.sym: A loud clicking or rattling for a few seconds every time the engine starts.
issues.why: A dealer diagnosed the timing chain tensioner losing its oil prime, so the chain is loose until oil pressure builds.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. A worn tensioner can let the chain wear guides or jump a tooth, which can badly damage the engine.

issues.t: Transmission shudders
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration while accelerating or cruising, often felt at light throttle, at higher mileage.
issues.why: Owners report shudder from the six-speed automatic, which commonly comes from torque converter or internal transmission wear.
issues.next: Have the transmission fluid checked and the car scanned for codes. A software update or fluid change may help early; severe cases need a rebuild.

issues.t: Power steering assist can suddenly shut off (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets very heavy, especially at low speed, and a warning may appear.
issues.why: A sensor fault in the electric steering motor can turn off power assist. The recall covers 2011-2012 EcoBoost cars and all 2013 MKS models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Electric power steering gear fails
issues.sym: Steering assist goes away and the wheel becomes very hard to turn, often with a power steering warning.
issues.why: Owners report the electric steering gear itself failing at around 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Drive carefully and have the steering system diagnosed. The fix is usually a new steering gear.

issues.t: Wheel bearings hum or growl
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: The wheel hub bearings wear out, with owners reporting it around 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noise traced to the right corner. A failing bearing should be replaced before it gets loose.

issues.t: Front brakes grind or wear out early
issues.sym: Grunting or grinding from the front brakes, or pads and rotors that wear out sooner than expected.
issues.why: RepairPal lists front brake grunting and grinding as a known MKS complaint, and owners also report early brake wear on this heavy sedan.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured. Grinding can mean metal-on-metal contact, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Sunroof opens by itself
issues.sym: The sunroof opens on its own while parked or driving, which can let rain in.
issues.why: Owners report the sunroof opening unintentionally, which points to a fault in the switch, motor or control module.
issues.next: Close it and keep the car covered. Have the switch and motor checked.

issues.t: Car shuts down while driving
issues.sym: The engine and electrical systems shut off while driving, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report sudden shutdowns on the 2013 model, which are often electrical faults.
issues.next: Get to a safe place. Record when it happens and have the dealer check for codes and related service bulletins.

issues.t: Cabin temperature swings too hot or cold on its own
issues.sym: The climate control will not hold the set temperature and keeps blowing too hot or too cold.
issues.why: Owners report the automatic climate control drifting, usually from a blend door actuator or temperature sensor fault.
issues.next: Have the climate system scanned for codes and the actuators tested.

issues.t: Power door locks act up
issues.sym: Doors will not lock or unlock with the switch or fob, or lock and unlock by themselves.
issues.why: A failing door lock actuator inside the door is the usual cause.
issues.next: Find which door is acting up and have its actuator replaced.

issues.t: Dash touch controls stop working
issues.sym: The touch-sensitive controls for climate and audio on the center stack stop responding.
issues.why: Owners report the front control interface module (the touch panel) failing around 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Try a battery reset or software update first. If it stays dead, the panel module may need replacing.

issues.t: Air conditioning stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, sometimes with low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report A/C failures on the 2014 model. Common causes are refrigerant leaks or compressor and control faults.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressure-tested and checked for leaks before simply recharging it.

issues.t: Driver seatback will not stay upright
issues.sym: The driver seatback flops back or will not lock in position.
issues.why: Owners report the plastic part that holds the seatback angle breaking.
issues.next: Do not drive if the seatback will not hold. A dealer can replace or reinforce the recliner mechanism.

issues.t: Driver airbag may inflate wrongly in a severe crash (recall)
issues.sym: There are usually no symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: The driver front airbag may not inflate correctly during the second stage of deployment in a high-speed crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Driver airbag second-stage fault on 2011 models (recall)
issues.sym: There are usually no symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: As on the 2009 model, the driver front airbag may not inflate properly in a high-speed crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Inside door handle may let a door open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: An inside door handle does not spring all the way back after use.
issues.why: A return spring in the inside door handle can come out of place, so the door could unlatch in a side impact.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel tank seam can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel dripping near the tank.
issues.why: A seam on the side of the fuel tank may not be fully sealed, making it weaker in a crash and able to leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel delivery module can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the car or fuel dripping near the rear seat area.
issues.why: The module on top of the fuel tank can crack and leak, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Child safety locks can switch off on their own (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door with the child lock set can be opened from inside.
issues.why: On some cars built in late 2012 the child lock can move from on to off without warning.
issues.next: Check that the child locks are on before each trip. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Halfshaft can slip out and cut drive to the wheels (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive while moving, or rolls when parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the halfshaft may not have been installed correctly, so the shaft can disengage.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can overheat and stall the EcoBoost (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: A part in the fuel pump electronic control module can overheat and cut power to the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel tank straps may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from under the rear of the car, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: On some cars built in July 2015 the fuel tank bolts were not tightened, so the straps can break and the tank can drop.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: Parking brake may not fully hold (recall)
issues.sym: The car may roll on a slope with the parking brake set if it is not in Park.
issues.why: On some cars built in May 2015 the parking brake may not fully engage.
issues.next: Always shift into Park. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.
